title: RULES ON APPORTIONMENT OF COSTS FOR GRADE SEPARATION OF LEVEL CROSSINGS
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of these Rules is to prescribe matters necessary for apportioning the costs incurred in grade separation of railway crossings, pursuant to Article 8 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Promotion of Improvement of Railway Crossings. <Amended on August 3, 2006>

Article 2 (Scope of Application) When an existing railway crossing is converted into a grade-separated crossing, these Rules shall govern the allocation of costs between the road management authority and the railway infrastructure manager if the road concerned is a provincial road, Si road, Gun road, or Gu road under the Road Act, or a Myeon road, Ri road, or agricultural road under the Act on the Maintenance of Roads in Agricultural and Fishing Villages.

Article 3 (Standards for Apportionment of Costs) All expenses incurred in grade separation of a railway crossing, including construction costs and compensation expenses, shall be borne as follows: If the road concerned is a provincial road, the road management authority and the railway infrastructure manager shall each bear 50 percent of the expenses. If the road concerned is a Si road, Gun road, Gu road, Myeon road, Ri road, or agricultural road, the road management authority shall bear 25 percent and the railway infrastructure manager shall bear 75 percent. <Amended on August 3, 2006>

ADDENDUM <No. 481, June 10, 1974>
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDUM <No. 176, July 16, 2002>
These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

ADDENDUM <No. 340, August 3, 2006>
These Rules shall enter into force on the date of their promulgation.

metadata.completion_statement: All three main articles and all three supplied addenda are complete in English. The six existing English sections are assembled in source order, with limited corrections to the provincial-road category and the referenced rural-roads statute title.
